title: Passion fruit curd tart
subtitle: tangy tropical curd tart in a sweet pastry case
excerpt: Passion fruit curd tart is intensely sour and fragrant, the curd is made from strained passion fruit juice, eggs, butter, and sugar, cooked slowly until thick, then poured into a pre-baked pastry case. It sets to a firm, sliceable curd at room temperature. The flavour is more sharply tropical than lemon curd and the yellow colour is vivid against the pale pastry.
sourceNotes: Passion fruit curd is a relatively recent addition to the British home baking repertoire, following the same principles as lemon or lime curd but using the strained juice of passion fruit. Passion fruit are now consistently available in British supermarkets year-round. The curd-in-pastry-case format is directly borrowed from the lemon tart tradition, which has roots in both French tarte au citron and British lemon curd tarts. Strained passion fruit curd appears in Australian and New Zealand baking contexts from at least the 1980s, where passion fruit are widely grown.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the day before; the curd firms overnight and is easier to slice the next day.
recipe.temperatureNote: for blind baking the pastry case only; the curd is cooked on the hob

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: 190°C for blind baking the pastry case; the curd itself is cooked on the hob, not in the oven

content.text: Passion fruit curd tart is one of the most vivid and fragrant tarts you can make. The curd is bright yellow, intensely tropical, and sharp. It's poured into a fully baked pastry case and chilled to set firm. Use ripe, wrinkled passion fruit for the most concentrated juice, smooth-skinned ones are not yet ripe.

Make the pastry, chill, and roll to 3 mm. Line a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin and refrigerate 20 minutes. Blind bake at 190°C for 15 minutes with baking beans, then 10 minutes without until the case is dry, golden, and completely cooked through. Leave to cool.

Halve all the passion fruit and scoop the pulp into a sieve set over a bowl. Press firmly to extract the juice; discard the seeds. You need about 140 ml. Combine the juice, sugar, eggs, and egg yolks in a medium heavy-based saucepan. Cook over a low to medium heat, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, for 10 to 12 minutes until the curd has thickened to the consistency of double cream and coats the back of the spoon. Do not let it boil. Remove from the heat and stir in the cubed butter piece by piece until fully incorporated. Pour into the cooled pastry case and refrigerate for at least 2 hours until set.
